transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you—please have a seat. What brings you in today, and what would you like help with?

Lately I’ve been having a lot of trouble really listening when people talk to me, even when I’m trying to pay attention. My family and coworkers say I seem spaced out or like I’m not listening, and it’s starting to cause problems for me.

Do you also find yourself feeling tense or on edge and worrying a lot about different things most days, or is it more that your mind just drifts off or feels blank even when you’re not particularly worried?

It’s more that my mind drifts off or just kind of blanks, even when I don’t feel especially worried. I can be in the middle of a conversation and suddenly realize I’ve missed a chunk of what was said, without really knowing where my thoughts went.

Have you had similar problems with attention and seeming ‘spaced out’ since you were a child or teenager, for example in school, or is this a more recent change that started within the past few months to a year?

It’s been going on pretty much as long as I can remember, definitely since I was a kid in school. Teachers used to say I didn’t listen or that I “zoned out” in class, and I’d miss parts of instructions even when I was trying to pay attention.

Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling noticeably down, sad, or losing interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy most days, or has your mood been mostly okay despite the attention problems?

My mood has been mostly okay; I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling especially down or losing interest in things I usually like. I do get frustrated with myself about the attention issues, but overall I still enjoy my usual activities.

Besides feeling spaced out, do you also tend to be very fidgety, restless, or act on impulses quickly (like blurting things out or interrupting), or is it mainly the inattention and zoning out that causes you problems?

It’s both, honestly. I’m often really fidgety and have a hard time sitting still or doing quiet things without tapping or moving around, and I catch myself interrupting people or jumping into conversations before they’ve finished talking.

Do these attention and fidgeting problems cause significant difficulties for you in at least two different areas of your life, like both at work and at home or in relationships, and have they been pretty consistent over the years rather than coming and going in short phases?

Yeah, they cause problems both at work and at home. At work I miss parts of instructions, forget steps, and sometimes interrupt in meetings, and at home my partner gets annoyed because I zone out mid-conversation and cut people off without meaning to. It’s been like this pretty steadily for years, not just in short phases.

When you were a child or teenager, did these attention and fidgeting problems ever lead to things like needing special help at school, getting in trouble a lot, or struggling to keep up with homework and chores compared to other kids your age?

Yeah, I definitely struggled more than other kids with homework and chores—I’d start but not finish, or forget what I was supposed to be doing. Teachers often said I didn’t follow directions or wasn’t listening, and I’d get in trouble for that and for blurting things out or talking over other kids in class.

Thinking about your current difficulties, would you say the trouble paying attention and zoning out causes you more problems overall than the fidgeting and impulsive behaviors, or are the hyperactive and impulsive behaviors just as big a problem as the inattention?

I’d say the attention and zoning out causes me a bit more trouble overall, especially with missing instructions at work and spacing out during important conversations at home. The fidgeting and interrupting are definitely issues too, but the not-listening and losing track of what I’m supposed to be doing seem to get me into more serious problems.

Do you regularly use alcohol, cannabis, or any other drugs, or take any prescription medications that affect your thinking, and if so have your attention and fidgeting problems changed noticeably with their use?

I drink socially maybe once or twice a week, but not heavily, and I haven’t noticed it really changing my attention or fidgeting, aside from feeling a bit sluggish if I overdo it. I don’t use cannabis or other drugs, and I’m not on any prescription medications that affect my thinking.

Right now in your adult life, do the fidgeting, restlessness, and impulsive behaviors (like interrupting or acting before thinking) cause you just as much difficulty as the inattention, or are they clearly less of a problem day to day?

They’re a problem, but definitely less than the inattention. The biggest issues day to day are still missing parts of conversations and not following through on tasks, whereas the fidgeting and interrupting mostly just annoy people or make me feel self‑conscious rather than completely derailing things.
